en.text: Physalis heterophylla, colloquial name clammy groundcherry, is species of herbaceous plant in the family Solanaceae. It is native to North America, occurring primarily in the eastern United States and Canada. It is known to occur in all contiguous states except for Nevada and California. It is found mainly in habitats such as dry or mesic prairies, gravel hills and rises, sandy or rocky soils, and waste places such as roadsides.

fr.text: Physalis heterophylla, le coqueret hétérophylle ou cerise de terre sauvage, est une plante vivace appartenant au genre Physalis et à la famille des Solanaceae. La plante est surtout connue pour son fruit, baie comestible de couleur orangée enfermée dans un calice jaune verdâtre semblable à une lanterne.

en.heading: Toxicity
en.text: Outside of the mature fruit, which is edible, all parts of P. heterophylla contain toxic amounts of solanine, which is poisonous to humans and animals. Symptoms of solanine poisoning include headache, stomach pain, lowered temperature, dilated pupils, vomiting, diarrhea, circulatory and respiratory depression, and loss of sensation.
